## Six columns, six meanings {#l2-four-columns .compact}

| Column | What it represents |
|:---|:---|
| Value, $x$ | The number of pets in a household |
| Frequency, $f$ | How many households have exactly this value |
| Product, $fx$ | The total number of pets contributed by those households |
| Cumulative frequency, $cf$ | How many households have this value or a smaller one |
| Relative frequency, $rf=f/n$ | The proportion with exactly this value |
| Cumulative relative frequency, $crf=cf/n$ | The proportion with this value or a smaller one |

::: {.takeaway}
Order the values first. The final $cf$ is $n$; the final $crf$ is $1$.
:::

::: notes
Use the shared Example3.4 dataset to connect every symbol to a meaning. Atx=1, f=20, fx=20, cf=35, rf=.40 and crf=.70. Equal-looking entries need not count the same thing: f counts households, while fx counts pets. For grouped intervals the running total at an upper boundary means values below that boundary under the stated a≤x<b convention.
:::
